title: MacKenzie Scott helped abolish $40B in medical debt; how mechanics work
content: MacKenzie Scott is leading the charge in medical debt relief, having made groundbreaking donations that freed over $40 billion for families burdened by this often overwhelming responsibility. Yet, the call for broader policy reform lingers, revealing the constraints of this philanthropic model.

title: Awarapan 2 box office day 1: Emraan Hashmi starrer opens at Rs 27 crore
content: Emraan Hashmi's 'Awarapan 2' has achieved a strong opening at the Indian box office. The film earned an estimated Rs 21 crore net on its first day. This collection marks Emraan Hashmi's biggest opening day at the box office. The sequel significantly surpassed the original 'Awarapan's' opening day earnings. Advance bookings and walk-in audiences contributed to the film's successful debut.

title: Oracle prepares fresh layoffs before September 1, asks managers to name who goes
content: Oracle is planning fresh layoffs this month, with managers reportedly asked to identify employees whose roles will go before its second fiscal quarter opens on September 1. Some teams face double-digit percentage cuts. The move follows a year in which Oracle eliminated 21,000 jobs, spent $1.8 billion on restructuring, and poured $55.7 billion into AI data centres.

title: Berlin Volksbühne cancels ‘Black people only’ pool event after backlash
content: Berlin’s Volksbuhne swimming pool has cancelled a planned event exclusively for Black communities after facing backlash over restricted access. The €300,000 temporary pool was due to close to the general public for six hours on August 14. Organisers cited security concerns, saying Black children and teenagers had faced right-wing and racist harassment at swimming events.

title: Europe battles self-cloning crayfish as Czech Republic targets new outbreaks
content: European conservationists are launching a campaign to eradicate new populations of marbled crayfish, notorious for their rapid reproduction and the deadly diseases they carry. Funded by the European Union, these swift action initiatives aim to tackle invasive species promptly, mitigating the risk of extensive environmental and economic harm while safeguarding native ecosystems from foreign invaders.

title: Zohran Mamdani’s ‘common sense regulation’ may push Amazon to move NYC deliveries

However, Amazon has raised concerns, indicating the bill may drive its operations outside of the city.

title: Batwara 1947 opens at Rs 5.75 crore, trails behind Awarapan 2
content: 'Batwara 1947', a partition-themed drama starring Sunny Deol, hit the big screens on Friday, garnering an impressive Rs 5.75 crore net on its opening day. With overseas collections of Rs 1.50 crore, the film aims for a robust worldwide gross. It faces tough competition from both 'Awarapan 2' and 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day', while also signaling the return of Preity Zinta to cinema after eight years.

title: What happened to Goldberg after WWE? Inside his life and new business ventures
content: Bill Goldberg has transitioned into a busy post-wrestling career after retiring in 2025. He is now focusing on executive business, leadership, and automotive projects. Goldberg is also involved in television shows and family projects with his son. He co-owns Patriot Tactical, a company specializing in self-defense equipment and gear. The wrestling legend continues to pursue his passion for American muscle cars and custom vehicle restoration.

A championship win could further boost his financial standing and career opportunities.

Discover abandoned camps filled with loot and exploration maps, while new furniture blocks like wool cushions and straw beds enable enhanced building creativity. Additionally, the introduction of concrete slabs and stairs diversifies design possibilities, creating an inviting and adventure-friendly gaming experience.

title: Gandhi's letter to India, as told through TOI
content: From his South Africa years to the freedom struggle, Mahatma Gandhi repeatedly used newspapers to address India’s public. Alok Sharma sifts through letters Gandhi wrote to TOI, illuminating his positions on Satyagraha, the Rowlatt Act, Dalit representation, Hindu-Muslim unity and the hardships faced by Indians in South Africa.

title: ‘This house is mine’: Bengaluru couple’s fight ends in wife’s murder, man’s suicide

He mentioned an argument with his wife, Padmavathi, before his death.  Padmavathi's family has accused her husband of murder and subsequent suicide.  Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding their deaths.

title: 'Like coming home': German Ambassador Jasper Wieck recalls 35-year India journey
content: German Ambassador Jasper Wieck reflects on his long-standing friendship with India, illustrated through personal photographs from trips he embarked on nearly thirty-five years ago. These snapshots highlight a simpler era, capturing the essence of India’s monuments and vibrant streets. Each image tells a story of unexpected friendships and everyday moments that remind us that travel memories can often extend beyond mere tourist attractions.

title: 'India can take risks, hit hard': NSA says message to world clear after Op Sindoor
content: National Security Adviser Ajit Doval conveyed India's strong stance against adversaries.  Operation Sindoor was launched after a terror attack in Pahalgam.  India conducted precision strikes on terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-administered Kashmir.  The operation demonstrated India's military superiority and willingness to act decisively.  This action concluded an 88-hour conflict, forcing Pakistan to seek peace.

title: Cockroaches, expired food: FDA suspends licences of Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart hubs
content: The Maharashtra FDA took decisive action by suspending licenses for fourteen food outlets affiliated with quick-commerce services like Blinkit and Zepto, citing significant hygiene breaches. Inspections uncovered problems in pest management, storage conditions, and temperature regulation. In response, some establishments were temporarily closed, while others received official notices to rectify non-compliance, highlighting the urgent need for online food operators to maintain strict safety standards.

title: ‘Don’t play politics with me’: CJP’s Ranka confronts cop, cites Pradhan’s ouster

title: 'I shot him': Luigi Mangione pleads guilty to killing United Healthcare CEO
content: Luigi Mangione has confessed to the fatal shooting of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson in Manhattan. He has entered a guilty plea for federal stalking charges in connection to the incident. This plea addresses one of two criminal cases targeting Mangione, while he is still preparing for a state murder trial set for September. During the investigation, authorities found a 3D-printed gun along with a notebook.

title: Marcus Aurelius' quote on how perception shapes what we hear and see
content: Marcus Aurelius, the philosopher-king of Rome, turned to Stoicism as a means to master the trials of existence. He championed the ability to control one's own reactions, urging acceptance of circumstances beyond personal control. His focus on virtue over fleeting fame, wealth, or power is vividly captured in his reflections, Meditations, which continue to provide valuable insights for overcoming life's challenges and uncertainties.

title: LS panel sends notice to Rahul over 'unparliamentary' remarks against Shah
content: Rahul Gandhi has been served a Lok Sabha notice regarding privilege complaints raised by BJP MPs Anurag Thakur and Sanjay Jaiswal. The complaints accuse Gandhi of using inappropriate and disrespectful language towards Amit Shah. He is required to submit a response to the Secretariat by August 28, after which the Speaker will assess both the complaints and his reply.

title: Brunei Sultan strips daughter-in-law of royal title over 'unbecoming conduct'
content: Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah of Brunei has stripped daughter-in-law Pengiran Raabi’atul Adawiyyah of her royal title over conduct deemed “unbecoming” of a royal spouse. The palace said her actions tarnished the monarchy’s reputation and showed disrespect towards the Sultan. Raabi’atul remains married to Prince Abdul Malik, with no divorce announced, while their four daughters retain their titles.

title: Male redback spiders somersault directly towards a female’s fangs during mating
content: Recent research uncovers that a singular genetic region governs the intricate somersaulting behavior of male redback spiders during mating rituals. This fascinating behavior, crucial for reproduction, is inherited through the X chromosome. Experimental hybrids indicate that this somersault characteristic is not only recessive but also X-linked. Conversely, abdominal narrowing seems influenced by a combination of multiple genes and environmental conditions, challenging traditional views on the complexity of genetic traits.

title: Pew survey: What US, UK and others think about India at 80
content: India's standing on the global stage reveals a mixed bag of perceptions among nations, with only 45% viewing it favorably. While Pakistan's outlook remains critical, Sri Lanka showcases significant support. Since 2025, favorability has waned in several countries, yet noteworthy improvements have emerged in Germany and the UK, highlighting the complexities and challenges of India's international reputation.

title: Naomi Osaka on motherhood: How self-care changed her approach to parenting

After becoming a mother, Osaka re-entered the tennis world, seeking to harmonize her dual identity.

title: Savarkar remark: Supreme Court quashes case against Rahul Gandhi
content:
Rahul had allegedly described Savarkar as a “receiver of pension from Britishers” and “a servant of Britishers” at a news conference in 2022.

Noting that there was no sanction to prosecute leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha Gandhi for his remarks against V D Savarkar, Supreme Court Friday quashed proceedings against him initiated by a Lucknow court. Rahul had allegedly described Savarkar as a "receiver of pension from Britishers" and "a servant of Britishers" at a news conference in 2022. SC, which had given an earful to Rahul at the last hearing, concluded that criminal proceedings against him were untenable for want of sanction. A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu allowed Rahul's appeal on the ground of lack of sanction, even before senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi could argue the case on behalf of the Congress MP.

End of Article

title: Two American jets with same flight number avoid mid-air disaster
